CVE-2026-100691.description: Hugo versions 0.75.0 through 0.165.x contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability: the syntax highlighter does not escape the `lineAnchors` option before passing it to Chroma, which writes the value verbatim into the `id` and `href` attributes of the generated line-number markup. A crafted `lineAnchors` value supplied as a Markdown code fence attribute (or passed to the `highlight` template function) results in unescaped HTML in the rendered page, allowing arbitrary JavaScript to execute in the browsers of visitors to the generated site. This affects sites that build and publish Markdown from untrusted contributors; Hugo's security model otherwise considers content trusted input. Fixed in 0.166.0, where the `lineAnchors` value is HTML-escaped before being passed to Chroma.

CVE-2026-100692.description: Hugo is a static site generator. In versions after v0.123.0 and before v0.166.0, Hugo's symlink confinement checks stopped at the mount root itself, so a theme or module checked into themes/ (or a vendored module) could contain a symlink at a mount root (for example themes/mytheme/assets -> /some/dir/outside). Files behind such a symlink were readable during a site build through resources.Get, resources.Match and similar functions, and could be published to public/ via static mounts, bypassing the rule that theme and module mount sources must be local paths. Modules fetched via Go modules are not affected because Go module zips cannot contain symlinks, and this is not an escalation for the main project, which may already mount absolute paths by configuration. Fixed in v0.166.0, where symlinked mount roots and symlinked directories between the mount root and the module directory are treated as non-existent for all modules. As a workaround, inspect themes/ and vendored modules for symlinks at mount roots before building, or replace symlinks with explicit mounts.

CVE-2026-100694.title: Hugo is a static site generator. In versions from v0.56.0 through ...
CVE-2026-100694.description: Hugo is a static site generator. In versions from v0.56.0 through v0.165.x, content files mapped to the text/org media type are rendered without escaping raw HTML: Org export blocks and @@html:...@@ snippets pass HTML through unescaped, resulting in cross-site scripting (XSS) in the generated site. An attacker who can supply or influence a content file under /content or the output of a content adapter can inject scripts that execute in the browsers of visitors to the affected pages. Only pages whose source file or content-adapter output declares the text/org media type are affected, and sites that fully trust all content sources are not impacted. Version v0.166.0 fixes the issue by introducing a security.allowContent allowlist that denies text/org by default; sites that intentionally author Org Mode content can opt back in with [security] allowContent = ['.*'].

CVE-2026-10582.title: Hugo's security.http.urls allowlist is the only control on outbou ...
CVE-2026-10582.description: Hugo's security.http.urls allowlist is the only control on outbound fetches made by resources.GetRemote, and it inspects the URL text alone. CheckAllowedHTTPURL in config/security/securityConfig.go applies the configured pattern list and then re-checks a canonicalised form of an integer, hex or octal IPv4 host, but it never resolves the hostname and never inspects the address the HTTP client actually connects to. The client constructed in resources/resource_factories/create/create.go installs no dial-time hook, so no check occurs at connection time either. A hostname that resolves to a loopback, private or cloud-metadata address therefore satisfies the policy, and the response body is embedded in the generated site. An attacker who can supply a URL through content, for example a front-matter field or a CMS field, can make the build fetch an internal endpoint and publish the response in the static output, so the build artifact itself carries the data out.

CVE-2026-10618.description: Hugo's default fenced-code-block renderer writes attribute values taken from the code-fence info string into the rendered HTML without escaping them. New in markup/internal/attributes/attributes.go converts every attribute value from a byte slice to a string as it is stored, deliberately dropping the escaping that used to happen there, and RenderAttributes in the same file escapes only values that are still byte slices, so its escaping branch is never reached and every value is written verbatim. The function's documentation states that it performs HTML escaping of string attributes, which it does not. A quote inside an attribute value in the info string therefore terminates the attribute and allows a further attribute, including an event handler, to be placed on the wrapper element, and the script runs for every visitor who loads the page. This path is reached under the default configuration, with code fences enabled and without goldmark's unsafe setting or any custom render hook. Attribute names beginning with on are filtered when the attributes are parsed, so injection is achieved through the value rather than the name.

CVE-2026-50134.description: Hugo is a static site generator. From 0.91.0 until 0.162.0, resources.GetRemote enforces security.http.urls on the URL it is called with, but it did not re-validate intermediate URLs on HTTP 3xx redirects. An allowed server (or an attacker controlling its DNS or response) could therefore redirect the request to a host that the policy was meant to forbid and Hugo would fetch from the redirected target. The same bypass also lifted any host-shape restriction the operator had put in place. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.162.0.

This issue is fixed in v0.163.1.

CVE-2026-89258.description: Hugo is a static site generator. This issue is an incomplete-fix follow-up to GHSA-c3wq-j5vh-68rc and GHSA-fw87-fv5r-9fpw; it is fixed in v0.165.0.

CVE-2026-89259.description: Hugo is a static site generator. GHSA-3jfr-vjcq-7jvf.title: css.Sass allowed themes to read files outside the project via the Sass compiler's import fallback
GHSA-3jfr-vjcq-7jvf.description: ### Summary Hugo's security model states that only the main project, not external components such as themes, can access files outside the project root. `css.Sass` resolved `@import` and `@use` targets not found in Hugo's virtual file system by handing them to the Sass compiler (Dart Sass or LibSASS), with the real mount directories as include paths. The compiler reads directly from the file system with no notion of the project root and follows symlinks. A theme could ship a stylesheet with `@import '../../../../secret';`, an absolute path, or a symlink pointing outside the project, and have the file content compiled into the published CSS. ### Impact A malicious theme or Hugo module can read Sass and CSS files, or via a symlink any file, readable by the build user and publish the content as part of the site's CSS. No user interaction beyond using the theme and running a build is required. ### Patches Fixed in v0.167.0. Imports not found in Hugo's virtual file system are now resolved by Hugo and checked against the working directory and the paths in `security.node.permissions.allowRead`; anything that resolves outside these, including via symlinks, fails the build. This applies to both the Dart Sass and the LibSASS transpiler. ### Workarounds Do not use themes or modules you do not trust. Review `@import` and `@use` statements in `css.Sass` entry points for paths that leave the project. ### References * [Hugo's Security Model](https://gohugo.io/about/security/) * [`security.node.permissions.allowRead`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/security/#nodepermissionsallowread) Thanks to @Hama1cco for finding and reporting this issue.

GHSA-6c8w-mpp8-9w47.title: Symlink in nested-mount ancestor directory of a theme exposes files outside the module
GHSA-6c8w-mpp8-9w47.description: ### Impact When a module mount is nested below another mount (e.g. `assets` and `assets/vendor/x`), Hugo enumerates the intermediate 'virtual ancestor' directory (`assets/vendor`) by joining the path onto the parent mount and calling `Stat`, which follows symlinks. This path did not apply the symlink confinement rules used elsewhere in the root mapping filesystem. A malicious or compromised theme/module can place a symlink (or NTFS junction) at that ancestor directory pointing outside its own root. Files from the link target are then listed by `resources.Match` and similar, and their content is readable during the build, so it can end up in the published output. The attacker must control a theme/module used by the victim site. Impact is limited to local file disclosure during the build. ### Affected versions All versions up to and including v0.166.0. The affected code path dates back to v0.64.1; the symlink confinement it bypasses was introduced in v0.162.0 through v0.166.0. ### Patches Fixed in v0.167.0. The virtual-ancestor lookup now rejects entries that are symlinks or have a symlinked parent below the mount root, matching the existing rules for direct file access. ### Workarounds Do not use themes or modules from untrusted sources. Inspect vendored themes for symlinks or junctions in mounted directories before building. ### References - CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

GHSA-797m-7j5g-3rpr.title: Symlinked mount roots in themes/modules could read files outside the module
GHSA-797m-7j5g-3rpr.description: ### Impact Hugo's symlink confinement checks stopped at the mount root itself. A theme or module checked into `themes/` could therefore contain a symlink at a mount root (for example `themes/mytheme/assets -> /some/dir/outside`), and files behind it were readable through `resources.Get`, `resources.Match` and similar functions, and could be published to `public/` via `static` mounts. This bypassed the rule that theme and module mount sources must be local paths, which is part of Hugo's [security model](https://gohugo.io/about/security/): only the main project may access files outside the project root. Modules fetched via Go modules are not affected, as Go module zips cannot contain symlinks. The main project could already mount absolute paths by configuration, so this is not an escalation there. ### Patches Fixed in v0.166.0. Symlinked mount roots, and symlinked directories between the mount root and the module directory, are now treated as non-existent for all modules, the main project included. Absolute mount sources in the main project continue to work. ### Workarounds Inspect `themes/` and vendored modules for symlinks at mount roots before building, or replace symlinks with explicit mounts. ### References - Related: GHSA-vrv5-r5rf-6v4j, GHSA-c3wq-j5vh-68rc, GHSA-fw87-fv5r-9fpw

GHSA-q4xf-287f-98r8.title: Stored XSS via unescaped lineAnchors code block option
GHSA-q4xf-287f-98r8.description: ### Impact Hugo's syntax highlighter did not escape the `lineAnchors` option before passing it to Chroma, which writes the value verbatim into the `id` and `href` attributes of the generated line number markup. A `lineAnchors` value supplied as a code fence attribute in Markdown content, e.g. ````markdown ```go {lineNos=true anchorLineNos=true lineAnchors='z\'><script>alert(1)</script>'} func main() {} ``` ```` resulted in unescaped HTML in the rendered page. This is a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability for sites that build and publish Markdown from untrusted contributors. The `highlight` template function is affected in the same way when given an untrusted `lineAnchors` option. ### Patches Fixed in v0.166.0. The `lineAnchors` value is now HTML-escaped before it is passed to Chroma. ### Workarounds None. If you cannot upgrade, do not build Markdown from untrusted sources. ### References Note that per [Hugo's security model](https://gohugo.io/about/security/), content is considered trusted input. This advisory is published for sites that nonetheless process untrusted Markdown.

GHSA-r73q-gwx2-fpxm.title: Theme-defined module.replacements bypass mount restrictions and widen the Node.js read sandbox
GHSA-r73q-gwx2-fpxm.description: ### Summary A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements` and mount directories anywhere on the host. ### Details A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements`. If the project didn't set any replacements, Hugo applied the theme's replacements as if the project had set them. The theme could then import and mount a directory anywhere on the host, either by absolute path or by escaping `themesDir` with `../`. This got around the rule that theme mount sources must be local paths. Mounting such a directory as `assets` also added it to the Node.js `--allow-fs-read` roots. That widened the `security.node.permissions` sandbox. For example, Node tools such as `css.PostCSS` could read files from that directory and load JavaScript modules from it. Only sites that use an untrusted theme or module are affected. ### Proof of concept Create a theme as outlined in the Go test below: ```go func TestMountRestrictThemeReplacements(t *testing.T) { files := ` -- hugo.toml -- disableKinds = ['taxonomy', 'term', 'rss'] theme = 'mytheme' -- themes/mytheme/hugo.toml -- [module] replacements = 'evil -> ../../secret' [[module.imports]] path = 'evil' [[module.imports.mounts]] source = '.' target = 'assets' -- secret/file1.txt -- file1 -- layouts/all.html -- All. ` b, err := hugolib.TestE(t, files) b.Assert(err, qt.IsNotNil) b.Assert(err.Error(), qt.Contains, `module 'evil' not found in '/themes/evil'`) } ``` ### Impact A theme could read file outside of its sandbox.

GHSA-vrm6-x8vp-mv2r.title: TailwindCSS needs elevated Node permissions
GHSA-vrm6-x8vp-mv2r.description: From v0.161.0, Hugo runs Node tools under Node's permission model. Unfortunately TailwindCSS needs a very permissive setup to work (`--allow-addons`, `--allow-child-process`, `--allow-worker`). We have gotten report from a security researcher who says that our fix for GHSA-x597-9fr4-5857 was incomplete, that it's still possible for a Node tool to e.g. read/write files outside outside the project's working directory. This was fixed in Hugo `v0.165.0` by removing `tailwindcss` from the default `security.exec.allow` list. Users who do not use TailwindCSS, or who only build trusted sites, are not affected. ### Workaround Add a `security.exec.allow` to your `hugo.toml` with only the external tools that you need. e.g.: ```toml [security.exec] allow = ['^(go|npx|babel|node|git)$'] ```

GHSA-vrv5-r5rf-6v4j.title: Symlink confinement bypass in resources.Get and os.ReadFile
GHSA-vrv5-r5rf-6v4j.description: Our fix for GHSA-c3wq-j5vh-68rc and GHSA-fw87-fv5r-9fpw was incomplete. Hugo `v0.165.0` hardened this by also dropping symlinks in parent directories. This required the attacker to be able to place (or convince a site author to place) a symlink inside a mounted directory — for example, inside a locally-vendored theme under themes/. Themes mounted as Go modules from GitHub have symlinks stripped on download and are not affected. Multi-directory walks (e.g. content/asset walking) were not affected either; only direct lookups via e.g. resources.Get followed symlinks.

GHSA-3jfr-vjcq-7jvf.description: ### Summary Hugo's security model states that only the main project, not external components such as themes, can access files outside the project root. `css.Sass` resolved `@import` and `@use` targets not found in Hugo's virtual file system by handing them to the Sass compiler (Dart Sass or LibSASS), with the real mount directories as include paths. A theme could ship a stylesheet with `@import '../../../../secret';`, an absolute path, or a symlink pointing outside the project, and have the file content compiled into the published CSS. ### Impact A malicious theme or Hugo module can read Sass and CSS files, or via a symlink any file, readable by the build user and publish the content as part of the site's CSS. No user interaction beyond using the theme and running a build is required. ### Patches Fixed in v0.167.0. Imports not found in Hugo's virtual file system are now resolved by Hugo and checked against the working directory and the paths in `security.node.permissions.allowRead`; anything that resolves outside these, including via symlinks, fails the build. This applies to both the Dart Sass and the LibSASS transpiler. ### Workarounds Do not use themes or modules you do not trust. Review `@import` and `@use` statements in `css.Sass` entry points for paths that leave the project. ### References * [Hugo's Security Model](https://gohugo.io/about/security/) * [`security.node.permissions.allowRead`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/security/#nodepermissionsallowread) Thanks to @Hama1cco for finding and reporting this issue.

GHSA-6c8w-mpp8-9w47.description: ### Impact When a module mount is nested below another mount (e.g. `assets` and `assets/vendor/x`), Hugo enumerates the intermediate 'virtual ancestor' directory (`assets/vendor`) by joining the path onto the parent mount and calling `Stat`, which follows symlinks. This path did not apply the symlink confinement rules used elsewhere in the root mapping filesystem. A malicious or compromised theme/module can place a symlink (or NTFS junction) at that ancestor directory pointing outside its own root. Files from the link target are then listed by `resources.Match` and similar, and their content is readable during the build, so it can end up in the published output. The attacker must control a theme/module used by the victim site. Impact is limited to local file disclosure during the build. ### Affected versions All versions up to and including v0.166.0. The affected code path dates back to v0.64.1; the symlink confinement it bypasses was introduced in v0.162.0 through v0.166.0. ### Patches Fixed in v0.167.0. The virtual-ancestor lookup now rejects entries that are symlinks or have a symlinked parent below the mount root, matching the existing rules for direct file access. ### Workarounds Do not use themes or modules from untrusted sources. Inspect vendored themes for symlinks or junctions in mounted directories before building. ### References - CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

GHSA-797m-7j5g-3rpr.title: Symlinked mount roots in themes/modules could read files outside the module
GHSA-797m-7j5g-3rpr.description: ### Impact Hugo's symlink confinement checks stopped at the mount root itself. Modules fetched via Go modules are not affected, as Go module zips cannot contain symlinks. The main project could already mount absolute paths by configuration, so this is not an escalation there. ### Patches Fixed in v0.166.0. Symlinked mount roots, and symlinked directories between the mount root and the module directory, are now treated as non-existent for all modules, the main project included. Absolute mount sources in the main project continue to work. ### Workarounds Inspect `themes/` and vendored modules for symlinks at mount roots before building, or replace symlinks with explicit mounts. ### References - Related: GHSA-vrv5-r5rf-6v4j, GHSA-c3wq-j5vh-68rc, GHSA-fw87-fv5r-9fpw

GHSA-q4xf-287f-98r8.title: Stored XSS via unescaped lineAnchors code block option
GHSA-q4xf-287f-98r8.description: ### Impact Hugo's syntax highlighter did not escape the `lineAnchors` option before passing it to Chroma, which writes the value verbatim into the `id` and `href` attributes of the generated line number markup. A `lineAnchors` value supplied as a code fence attribute in Markdown content, e.g. ````markdown ```go {lineNos=true anchorLineNos=true lineAnchors='z\'><script>alert(1)</script>'} func main() {} ``` ```` resulted in unescaped HTML in the rendered page. This is a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability for sites that build and publish Markdown from untrusted contributors. The `highlight` template function is affected in the same way when given an untrusted `lineAnchors` option. ### Patches Fixed in v0.166.0. The `lineAnchors` value is now HTML-escaped before it is passed to Chroma. ### Workarounds None. If you cannot upgrade, do not build Markdown from untrusted sources. ### References Note that per [Hugo's security model](https://gohugo.io/about/security/), content is considered trusted input. This advisory is published for sites that nonetheless process untrusted Markdown.

GHSA-r73q-gwx2-fpxm.title: Theme-defined module.replacements bypass mount restrictions and widen the Node.js read sandbox
GHSA-r73q-gwx2-fpxm.description: ### Summary A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements` and mount directories anywhere on the host. ### Details A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements`. If the project didn't set any replacements, Hugo applied the theme's replacements as if the project had set them. The theme could then import and mount a directory anywhere on the host, either by absolute path or by escaping `themesDir` with `../`. This got around the rule that theme mount sources must be local paths. Mounting such a directory as `assets` also added it to the Node.js `--allow-fs-read` roots. That widened the `security.node.permissions` sandbox. For example, Node tools such as `css.PostCSS` could read files from that directory and load JavaScript modules from it. Only sites that use an untrusted theme or module are affected. ### Proof of concept Create a theme as outlined in the Go test below: ```go func TestMountRestrictThemeReplacements(t *testing.T) { files := ` -- hugo.toml -- disableKinds = ['taxonomy', 'term', 'rss'] theme = 'mytheme' -- themes/mytheme/hugo.toml -- [module] replacements = 'evil -> ../../secret' [[module.imports]] path = 'evil' [[module.imports.mounts]] source = '.' target = 'assets' -- secret/file1.txt -- file1 -- layouts/all.html -- All. ` b, err := hugolib.TestE(t, files) b.Assert(err, qt.IsNotNil) b.Assert(err.Error(), qt.Contains, `module 'evil' not found in '/themes/evil'`) } ``` ### Impact A theme could read file outside of its sandbox.

CVE-2026-10582.description: Hugo's security.http.urls allowlist is the only control on outbound fetches made by resources.GetRemote, and it inspects the URL text alone. CVE-2026-10618.title: Hugo's default fenced-code-block renderer writes attribute values ...

Attribute names beginning with on are filtered when the attributes are parsed, so injection is achieved through the value rather than the name.

GHSA-q4xf-287f-98r8.title: Stored XSS via unescaped lineAnchors code block option

GHSA-r73q-gwx2-fpxm.description: ### Summary A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements` and mount directories anywhere on the host. ### Details A theme or module could define its own `module.replacements`. CVE-2026-10582.description: Hugo's security.http.urls allowlist is the only control on outbound fetches made by resources.GetRemote, and it inspects the URL text alone. CVE-2026-10618.title: Hugo's default fenced-code-block renderer writes attribute values ...
CVE-2026-10618.description: Hugo's default fenced-code-block renderer writes attribute values taken from the code-fence info string into the rendered HTML without escaping them.
